inline.text: Power of Siberia 2 Gas Pipeline (Russian: Сила Сибири - 2; Chinese: 西伯利亚力量-2号) is a proposed natural gas pipeline in Russia. The extension in Mongolia is referred to as Soyuz Vostok (Russian: Союз Восток).

The pipeline is proposed to run from the Bovanenkovovskoye and Kharasaveyskoye gas fields in Yamal, Russia through Urengoy, Krasnoyarsk Territory, Irkutsk Region, Buryatia and Transbaikalia. It would pass close to Lake Baikal, crossing the border of Mongolia, pass by Ulan Bator, and go on to China.

inline.text: Blue Stream Gas Pipeline (Russian: Голубой поток) is an operating natural gas pipeline in Russia and Turkey.

The pipeline runs from Izobilny, Stavropol Krai, Russia, through Beregovaya compressor station in Arkhipo-Osipovka, Krasnodar Krai, Russia, to the Durusu terminal in Turkey and then to Ankara, Turkey.
Operator: Gazprom, Blue Stream Pipeline B.V., BOTAŞ
Laid as low as 2.2 km (1.4 mi) undersea it is considered one of the deepest pipelines in the world.

candidates.context: ↑ 3.0 3.1 3.2 3.3 3.4 3.5 "Газопровод Голубой Поток" . energybase.ru . Retrieved 2022-08-03 . {{ cite web }} : CS1 maint: url-status ( link )

inline.text: The pipeline runs from Izobilny, Stavropol Krai, Russia, through Beregovaya compressor station in Arkhipo-Osipovka, Krasnodar Krai, Russia, to the Durusu terminal in Turkey and then to Ankara, Turkey.

The owners of the onshore segments of the gas pipeline in Russia and Turkey are Gazprom and Botas Petroleum Pipeline, respectively. The owner of the offshore segment and the Beregovaya compressor station is Blue Stream Pipeline Company B.V., which is owned by Eni and Gazprom.

The pipeline uses pipes with different diameters: mainland section 1,400 mm (55 in); mountainous section 1200 mm (47 in); and submarine section 610 mm (24 in). The gas pressure in the submarine section is 25 MPA (250 atm).

inline.text: Yamal-Europe Gas Pipeline (Russian: Газопровод "Ямал-Европа" ) is an operating gas pipeline (currently, idle), which transports gas from the Yamal Peninsula to European consumers, and travels across Russia, Belarus, Poland and Germany.

The 1,660 km-long gas pipeline can carry 33 billion cubic meters a year. It transports natural gas from the Yamal peninsula to European consumers. Construction began in 1994 and the pipeline was fully commissioned in 2006. The total cost was estimated around $36 billion.

The 402 km Russian segment starts from the Torzhok gas transmission hub in Tver Oblast. This section receives gas from the Northern Tyumen Regions (SRTO)–Torzhok Gas Pipeline . It consists of compressor stations at Rzhevskaya, Kholm-Zhirkovskaya and Smolenskaya.

The 575 km Belarusian section runs across Belarus and includes five compression stations, at Nesvizhskaya, Krupskaya, Slonimskaya, Minskaya and Orshanskaya. It passes through nearly 200 kilometers of bogs, 75 river crossings, 10 railways lines and three power transmission networks.

The Polish section is 683 km long and passes through 32 railway lines, 246 roads, streams and seven large rivers. This section also includes five compressor stations at Ciechanow, Szamotuly, Zambrow, Wloclawek and Kondratki.

The westernmost point of the gas pipeline is the Mallnow compressor station near Frankfurt an der Oder in the vicinity of the German-Polish border. inline.text: TransSakhalin Gas Pipeline System , also known as Sakhalin II (Сахалин-2), in a network of operating gas pipelines in Russia.

The pipeline network runs from Piltun-Astokhskoye-A and Piltun-Astokhskoye-B fields, Nogliki District, Sakhalin Oblast, Russia, and Lunskoye field, to the LNG plant and an oil export terminal near Prigorodnoye, Sakhalin Oblast, Russia.
Segment I (gathering pipeline): 172 km (Piltun-Astokhskoye field landfall to the onshore processing facility (OPF) in the Nogliki district)
Segment II (transmission pipeline): 637 km (OPF to the LNG plant and the oil export terminal near Prigorodnoye)
Segment III(gathering pipeline): 7 km (Lunskoye field landfall to OPF)
Diameter: 20, 48, 30 in Segment I: 20 in Segment II: 48 in Segment III: 30 in

inline.text: The first phase is referred to as the Taas-Tumus - Yakutsk Gas Pipeline. It runs from Taas-Tumus (Tas-Tumus, Sakha Republic, Russia) to Yakutsk, Russia.

inline.heading: Phase II
inline.text: The second portion of the pipeline consists of three parallel segments that run from Mastakhskoye gas condensate field (Mastakh) to Yakutsk.

inline.heading: Phase III
inline.text: The third portion of the pipeline consists of two parallel segments running from Srednevilyuyskoye gas condensate field, near the town of Kysyl-Syr in Vilyuysky District to Mastakh.

inline.heading: Kysyl-Syr - Mastakh Expansion
inline.text: This project is an 84-kilometer pipeline (third segment) running from Srednevilyuyskoye gas condensate field, near the town of Kysyl-Syr in Vilyuysky District to to Mastakh.

inline.heading: Phase I
inline.text: The first phase is referred to as the Taas-Tumus - Yakutsk Gas Pipeline. It runs from Taas-Tumus (Tas-Tumus, Sakha Republic, Russia) to Yakutsk, Russia.

inline.heading: Phase II
inline.text: The second portion of the pipeline consists of three parallel segments that run from Mastakhskoye gas condensate field (Mastakh) to Yakutsk.

inline.heading: Phase III
inline.text: The third portion of the pipeline consists of two parallel segments running from Srednevilyuyskoye gas condensate field, near the town of Kysyl-Syr in Vilyuysky District to Mastakh.

inline.heading: Phase III: Kysyl-Syr - Mastakh I and II Gas Pipelines

inline.text: Power of Siberia 2 Gas Pipeline (Russian: Сила Сибири - 2; Chinese: 西伯利亚力量-2号) is a proposed natural gas pipeline in Russia. The extension in Mongolia is referred to as Soyuz Vostok (Russian: Союз Восток).

The pipeline is proposed to run from the Bovanenkovovskoye and Kharasaveyskoye gas fields in Yamal, Russia through Urengoy, Krasnoyarsk Territory, Irkutsk Region, Buryatia and Transbaikalia. It would pass close to Lake Baikal, crossing the border of Mongolia, pass by Ulan Bator, and go on to China.

inline.text: Power of Siberia 2 Gas Pipeline (Russian: Сила Сибири - 2; Chinese: 西伯利亚力量-2号) is a proposed natural gas pipeline in Russia. The extension in Mongolia is referred to as Soyuz Vostok (Russian: Союз Восток).

The pipeline is proposed to run from the Bovanenkovovskoye and Kharasaveyskoye gas fields in Yamal, Russia through Urengoy, Krasnoyarsk Territory, Irkutsk Region, Buryatia and Transbaikalia. It would pass close to Lake Baikal, crossing the border of Mongolia, pass by Ulan Bator, and go on to China.

inline.text: Srednevilyuyskoye Gas Condensate Field - Yakutsk Gas Pipeline (Russian: МГ Средневилюйское газоконденсатное месторождение – Якутск; МГ СВ ГКМ-Мастах-Якутск) is an operating gas pipeline network in Russia.

inline.heading: Phase I
inline.text: The first phase is referred to as the Taas-Tumus - Yakutsk Gas Pipeline. It runs from Taas-Tumus (Tas-Tumus, Sakha Republic, Russia) to Yakutsk, Russia.

inline.heading: Phase II
inline.text: The second portion of the pipeline consists of three parallel segments that run from Mastakhskoye gas condensate field (Mastakh) to Yakutsk.

inline.heading: Phase III
inline.text: The third portion of the pipeline consists of two parallel segments running from Srednevilyuyskoye gas condensate field, near the town of Kysyl-Syr in Vilyuysky District to Mastakh.

inline.heading: Kysyl-Syr - Mastakh Expansion
inline.text: This project is an 84-kilometer pipeline (third segment) running from Srednevilyuyskoye gas condensate field, near the town of Kysyl-Syr in Vilyuysky District to to Mastakh.

inline.text: Myldzhino-Vertikos Gas Pipeline (Russian: Газопровод "Мыльджино – Вертикос") is an operating gas pipeline in Russia.
The pipeline starts in Myldzhino, Tomsk region, and runs to Vertikos, Tomsk region, Russia.
The pipeline sources gas from the Myldzhinskoye, Severo-Vasyuganskoye, Kazakskoye, and Pindzhinskoye oil and gas fields and connects to the Nizhnevartovsk-Parabel-Kuzbass Gas Pipeline .
